chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from 'Ala' al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
"Any man who wishes to free his female slave and marry her, and make her manumission her dowry, may do so."
ai.seo_question: How can a master free his female slave and marry her with manumission as the dowry?
ai.summary: Reported from Imam al-Baqir (AS) in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the legal validity of *kitabah*-adjacent manumission where the slave girl’s freedom is directly exchanged for marriage. It highlights the Shia juristic view that emancipation and nuptial contract can be unified, reflecting the social elevation of *Ummahat al-Awlad* (mothers of children) in early Islamic society. This mechanism underscores the flexibility in marital economics, allowing the master to retain the economic value of the bride price through the act of freeing her.
